name: Future continuous and future perfect
subtitle: Will be doing shows what is in progress at a future time: At nine tomorrow I will be sitting my exam. Will have done shows what is finished by a future time: By Friday I will have finished the report. Will have been doing shows how long something has lasted by then.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-c1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: At nine tomorrow I will be sitting my exam. — By Friday I will have finished the report. — In May we will have been living here for ten years.

qa.html: Future continuous: will be + -ing. Something will be in progress at a future moment: This time tomorrow I will be lying on a beach. It is also a polite way to ask about plans: Will you be using the car tonight? (It sounds less pushy than Are you going to use the car?)

Future perfect: will have + past participle. Something will be finished before a future time. Look for by, by then, by the time, before: By Friday I will have finished the report. She will have left by the time you arrive.

Future perfect continuous: will have been + -ing. It shows how long something has lasted up to a future point: In May we will have been living here for ten years. When the train comes, she will have been waiting for an hour.

Time clauses use the present. After by the time, when, before, after, as soon as, until do not use will: By the time she arrives, we will have left. The present perfect is also possible: By the time she has arrived…

A short point: guessing. will have + past participle can also be a confident guess about the past or about now: You'll have heard the news by now. (I expect you have.) This is fairly formal and polite.

Typical mistakes: ✗ By the time she will arrive, we'll have left. → ✓ By the time she arrives, we'll have left. · ✗ I will have been finished by six. → ✓ I will have finished by six. · ✗ At nine tomorrow I will have worked in the garden. (it is in progress) → ✓ At nine tomorrow I will be working in the garden.

concept.noteHtml: Spoken forms: I'll be working, I'll have finished, she won't have left. In everyday speech people often use a simpler form: I'll be done by Friday. The long forms are common in reports and plans. Basic future forms (will, going to, present continuous) are in Future forms. For time clauses see Time clauses. For guesses with must have and might have see Modals of deduction.

listen.text: At nine tomorrow I'll be sitting my driving test.
listen.note: Future continuous: it is in progress at nine.

listen.text: By Friday I'll have finished the report.
listen.note: Future perfect: it is finished by Friday.

listen.text: You'll have heard the news by now.
listen.note: A confident guess: I expect you have heard it.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose what you hear. Listen for be + -ing (in progress) and have + past participle (finished).

items.text: This time next week we'll be lying on a beach.
By six o'clock I'll have cooked dinner.
Will you be using the car tonight?
She'll have left by the time you arrive.
In June we'll have been married for ten years.
He'll be waiting at the station.

rounds.label: 1 · In progress: this time tomorrow
rounds.instruction: You hear what is happening now. Say that it will be in progress this time tomorrow. Use will be + -ing.

example.answer: This time tomorrow I will be flying to Rome.

items.answer: This time tomorrow Tom will be driving to Leeds.

items.prompt: We are sitting in the garden.
items.answer: This time tomorrow we will be sitting in the garden.
This time tomorrow Amira will be taking her exam.
This time tomorrow I will be lying on the beach.
This time tomorrow they will be travelling to Spain.
This time tomorrow Kwame will be giving a talk.

rounds.label: 2 · Finished by then: will have + past participle
rounds.instruction: You hear a plan and a time. Say that it will be finished by that time. Start with by.

example.answer: By Friday I will have finished the report.

items.answer: By Monday she will have written the essay.

items.prompt: We paint the kitchen. The weekend.
items.answer: By the weekend we will have painted the kitchen.
By June he will have read the book.
By September they will have sold the house.

items.prompt: I clean the flat. Six o'clock.
items.answer: By six o'clock I will have cleaned the flat.
By 2030 Zofia will have finished her degree.

exercises.title: Make the future perfect.
exercises.hint: A plan with by becomes will have + past participle.

exercises.title: Continuous, perfect or time clause?
exercises.hint: In progress at a time: will be -ing. Finished by a time: will have + past participle. After by the time: present.

exercises.title: Complete the verb form.
exercises.hint: will have + past participle. will be + -ing. will have been + -ing.

exercises.title: What does it say?
exercises.hint: will be -ing = in progress. will have + pp = finished. will have been -ing = how long. A guess says what you expect is true.

exercises.title: What goes together?
exercises.hint: Tap the situation, then the sentence that fits it.

exercises.title: Gap text: An email before a conference.
exercises.hint: Choose the form that fits: in progress, finished, how long, or a present tense after by the time.
